main_text.p: hoc putidum profert mendacium, non au-tem ex Orientalium monumentis. Often-damus, & primo ex Græcorum, seu Mel-chitarum Symbolicis scriptis.
Melchitæ in Menologio, sub dieno-na Iunij hoc de sancto Cyrillo Archiepis-copo Alexandriæ recitant Troparium.

p.i: Extitisti, o divino inflammate amore, Cyrille, director ad fidem Orthodoxam, Doctor illustris Religionis, Dux ad puritatem, & CYNOSURA Orbi habitabili, ac decus Principibus Sacerdotum, o Sapiens divine, documentisque tuis illuminasti Universum cognitione Spiritus. Quamobrem intercede apud Christum Deum pro salute animarum nostrarum. En Cynosura, Hottingere. Quo etiam titulo decoratur ibidem S. Gregorius Archiepiscopus Arme-

page.notes: Six lines of Arabic verse, centred, could not be read letter by letter at this scan resolution; the counts given are approximate. The Latin italic passage is the printed translation of the Arabic troparion. "Often-" in the first paragraph is doubtful at the line end (possibly "Oft-"); reading kept as the scan shows it. Spelling "diuino" and "Vniuersum" was altered to v/u per the rules; the printed form is "diuino" and "Vniuersum". The paragraph ends on "Arme-" and continues on the next page.
